description: This minor course covers the terminologies of power quality problems in distribution systems and power converter-based products, the drawbacks, causes and mitigation methods of power quality problems, and the reduction in energy consumption by power quality improvement.

syllabus.title: Introduction to Power Quality and its Standards
syllabus.body: Overview of power quality, voltage and current-based power quality problems, power quality standards, EMC standards, loads that cause power quality problems, harmonic analysis.

syllabus.title: Harmonic Mitigation Using Passive Filters
syllabus.body: Classification, principle of operation, selection criteria, limitations, design of passive tuned filters for single and three-phase non-linear loads.

syllabus.title: Power Quality Improvement Using Active Filters
syllabus.body: Classification, principle of operation, control techniques for single-phase and three-phase shunt active power filters, design of single-phase and three-phase shunt and series active power filters.

syllabus.title: Design of Improved Power Quality Converters
syllabus.body: Classification, operating principle, design and simulation of single-phase and three-phase power factor corrected buck, boost and buck-boost converters in continuous conduction mode.

outcomes: Understand the concept of power quality and its standards.
Understand the causes and mitigation of power quality problems in distribution systems.
Understand the role of various passive and active filters for power quality improvement.
Design power factor corrected converters for efficiency improvement.
textbooks: Math H. Bollen, Understanding Power Quality Problems, John Wiley IEEE Press, 2000.
Roger C. Dugan, Mark McGranaghan, Surya Santoso and H. Wayne Beaty, Electrical Power Systems Quality, 3rd Edition, McGraw Hill, 2012.
Bhim Singh, Ambrish Chandra and Kamal Al-Haddad, Power Quality Problems and Mitigation Techniques, Wiley, 2015.
referenceBooks: G. T. Heydt, Electric Power Quality, Stars in a Circle Publications, 1994.
